critique: The black background, orange-gold ember detail, and charcoal smoke are appropriate, and t1-to-t4 clearly shows particle motion. However, the result still reads as a small, symmetric explosion: a sharply defined circular orange ring with a dark center emits an evenly radial halo of sparks while the smoke expands as a round cloud. It lacks the thumbnail's dense, luminous, irregular flame mass and vertically rising smoke plume. The fire body is also too small and dim relative to the frame.

suggestions.why: Substantially reduce outward particle travel so the source can accumulate into a dense fire body instead of producing a broad radial explosion.
Increase upward acceleration to pull smoke and embers into a vertically rising plume rather than a symmetric circular cloud.
Raise emission density so the center reads as continuous luminous fire and smoke instead of a sparse ring of individually readable sprite particles.
Enlarge the clustered particle body so the fire/smoke occupies more of the frame and becomes the dominant form.
